title: Words of Spiritual Fortitude (Ki Ktien Ai Mynsiem)
cultural_context: Ballad of moral fortitude urging perseverance through winter cold, grief, and trials, from 'Ki Sur Pangnud Na Krem Shadem'.

khasi: Wat lwait, wat tlot, ko mynsiem,
Haba u slap u theh bad ka lyer ka suh;
Ka sngi kan mih biang pat ha u lum,
Ban pynkhie ia ka jingkyrmen thymmai;
Ki ktien ba ai mynsiem ki long
Kum ka um ba pynim ia u syntiew ba iap;
Ki pynskhem ia ki kjat ban iaid,
Sha khmat khlem da phai dien.
english: Faint not, falter not, O weary soul,
Though rain lashes down and winter winds chill;
The golden sun shall rise again above the mountain,
Like refreshing dew reviving a wilting blossom;
Strengthening the feet to walk firmly,

khasi: U Blei Um ju iehnoh ia uba bat hok,
U ieng ha syndah ban ai bor;
Man ka jingjynjar ka don la ka kut,
Ka jingshai kan jop ia ka miet;
To bat skhem ia ka jingngeit,
Ha dohnud to rwai ka sur kmen,
Ba ka jingim jong me kan long
Ka nuksa babha ia ka ri.
english: God never forsakes those who walk in truth,
Standing beside them to impart great strength;
Every tribulation has its ordained end,
The dawn of light shall vanquish the dark night;
Within your heart sing a melody of joy,
So that your life may shine
As an inspiring beacon for our motherland.
